title: Eagle Ford micro-balance
as_of_note: Current frame on EIA's October 2026 vintage. Production is EIA's combined crude plus lease condensate definition; the split into RRC categories does not exist in held data and the items say so.
units: kb/d unless a field name says otherwise

supply.label: Crude oil from oil leases (oil window)
supply.source: Texas RRC production by lease, product code 01 (not held)
supply.note: The larger share of the 1,110 combined total; the Karnes Trough core. The exact split does not exist in held data because the RRC pull does not exist in the library.

supply.label: Lease condensate from gas leases (condensate and wet-gas windows)
supply.source: Texas RRC production by lease, product code 03 (not held)
supply.note: The balance of the 1,110 combined total; historically a very large minority share in this basin. EIA carries only the combined figure.

supply.label: Austin Chalk and Buda overlay (memo, not additive)
supply.source: Texas RRC field-level data; operator disclosures
supply.note: A separate fractured carbonate target directly above the Eagle Ford, produced from many of the same pads and gathered into the same systems (EOG's Dorado is the named example). No held counter separates it. Carried as an explicit memo so the basin total is never silently inflated.

supply.label: Stabilized condensate reclassified at the stabilizer (memo)
supply.source: Company 10-K segment disclosures; no public throughput series
supply.note: Barrels that enter as gas-lease condensate and leave as a pipeline and export-legal product stream, the analogue of the WCSB's synthetic-to-blend line. Structure documented (EFS Midstream, WES Brasada and Springfield); volumes are not held. A subset of the condensate item above, never additive.

supply.label: Other South Texas conventional receipts
supply.note: Legacy fields along the corridor feeding the same systems. Small.

supply.label: Trucked receipts from outside gathering footprints (residual)
supply.note: The closure term on the supply side. Carried as a printed residual, never buried, once a flow layer exists.

demand.label: In-region refining (Three Rivers and Nixon)
demand.source: EIA capacity listings via Energy Factbook compilation
demand.note: Valero Three Rivers 89 plus Lazarus Energy Nixon at about 14. Runs are not separated from PADD 3 in public data.

demand.label: Eagle Ford JV Pipeline to Corpus Christi refining
demand.source: Plains and Enterprise disclosures; Form 6 filers held, schedule parse not built
demand.note: A share of the JV line's 660. The same steel south of Gardendale also carries Permian Cactus barrels: the basin's biggest line is partly occupied by another basin's oil.

demand.label: Eagle Ford JV Pipeline to the Eagle Ford Terminals dock
demand.source: Port of Corpus Christi; JV releases
demand.note: Loading rate 50,000 barrels per hour; about 1.4 MMbbl of storage. Loadings by origin basin are not public.

demand.label: Harvest system to Corpus refining
demand.dest: Corpus Christi refining and Three Rivers
demand.note: A share of the Arrowhead system total of 380. Harvest's own release names Flint Hills Corpus and Valero Three Rivers as destinations.

demand.label: Ingleside Pipeline to Ingleside marine terminals
demand.dest: Ingleside marine (EIEC, South Texas Gateway, Flint Hills)
demand.note: A terminal-delivery leg, fed by up to 380 of Harvest Eagle Ford barrels plus Permian connections. Not additive basin takeaway.

demand.label: Koch and Flint Hills system to Corpus
demand.dest: Corpus Christi refining and Ingleside dock
demand.source: Dated trade profiles; Flint Hills filings
demand.note: About 250 on dated trade profiles; treat as approximate. Flint Hills is primarily a purchaser and refiner system and public flow data is thin.

demand.label: NuStar South Texas system to Corpus
demand.source: NuStar Pipeline Operating Partnership files Form 6 (universe held)
demand.note: Capacity is not reliably published. The filer is in the held Form 6 universe; the schedule parse for this system is not built.

demand.label: Double Eagle Pipeline to Corpus
demand.note: Expandable to 150. Intrastate: absent from the Form 6 universe, so its flows live in Texas RRC data only. The basin's dedicated condensate line.

demand.label: Corpus Christi condensate splitters
demand.source: EIA capacity listing; company releases; Reuters
demand.note: Buckeye Texas Processing 60 (EIA-listed; two 25 kb/d trains by nameplate) plus Magellan, now ONEOK, 50. Splitter capacity is demand in this balance: it is where the lightest barrels clear. Runs are commercial data (Trafigura holds the throughput rights on both).

demand.label: KMCC to Houston Ship Channel
demand.dest: Houston Ship Channel (MEH, ECHO, Galena Park)
demand.note: In service June 2012. Intrastate: Kinder Morgan Crude and Condensate LLC does not appear in the 2022 to 2024 Form 6 universe. The Kinder Morgan Galena Park splitter (105) sits at this destination and is counted in the condensate processing group.

demand.label: KMCC Sweeny lateral to Phillips 66 Sweeny
demand.note: A lateral share of KMCC's 300. The Sweeny refinery's crude capacity is about 260 to 277 depending on the listing.

demand.label: Eagle Ford JV Lyssy interconnect to Houston (ECHO)
demand.note: A share of the JV line's 660. This interconnect is what makes Eagle Ford barrels swing between Corpus and Houston month to month.

demand.label: Permian trunk lines' Eagle Ford receipts to Corpus
demand.source: RBN Energy series built on Texas RRC pipeline data; GEM
demand.note: Cactus III (ex-EPIC) carries about 150 of designed Eagle Ford receipt capacity, with incidental receipts on Cactus I, Cactus II and Gray Oak. RBN's RRC-based series puts total transported volumes on the Permian-to-Corpus lines at about 2,560 to 2,650 including Eagle Ford receipts: Eagle Ford barrels are inside the Permian pipes' utilisation number.

demand.label: Balancing residual (truck, rail, other, measurement)
demand.note: Printed per the house rule, never buried. Expected small. It takes a value only when a flow layer exists to close against.

groups.label: Corpus Christi refining
groups.source: Group definitions per eagle_ford_dossier.md section 8 (overlapping roll-ups, not a partition)
groups.note: The adjacent refining pole, about 832 of crude capacity at Corpus proper.

groups.label: Corpus and Ingleside marine
groups.source: Group definitions per eagle_ford_dossier.md section 8 (overlapping roll-ups, not a partition)
groups.note: The export pole, about 2,400 of port loadings shared with Permian supply.

groups.label: Houston market
groups.source: Group definitions per eagle_ford_dossier.md section 8 (overlapping roll-ups, not a partition)

groups.label: Condensate processing
groups.source: Group definitions per eagle_ford_dossier.md section 8 (overlapping roll-ups, not a partition)
groups.note: The quality valve: splitter and stabilizer throughput is where the lightest barrels clear. Includes the Galena Park splitter (105) at the KMCC destination.

groups.label: Permian-shared infrastructure
groups.source: Group definitions per eagle_ford_dossier.md section 8 (overlapping roll-ups, not a partition)
groups.note: The group East Daley's format has no native slot for, and the one that decides this basin's realized economics.

prices.label: WTI at Magellan East Houston (MEH)
prices.source: ICE and Platts assessments (licensed, not held)
prices.note: The Gulf Coast light-sweet benchmark Eagle Ford barrels delivered to Houston price against. A Canadian producer's MD&A put the 2024 MEH premium at +$2.27/bbl over WTI Cushing, versus +$1.67 in 2023.

prices.label: WTI FOB Corpus Christi
prices.note: The waterborne assessment prices the export netback directly. The Corpus minus Houston spread is the basin's swing signal.

prices.label: Eagle Ford Crude (grade specification)
prices.note: 44.9 API, 0.12 percent sulphur. Very light and very sweet; at the light edge of refinery preference.

prices.label: Eagle Ford Condensate (grade specification)
prices.note: 54.9 API, 0.05 percent sulphur. Closer to natural gasoline than to a refinery's ideal crude; it clears through splitters, blending, or discount.

corridors.label: Eagle Ford to Corpus Christi
corridors.note: Short haul, about 100 to 200 miles. The corridor's real price is queue position at docks the Permian also claims. The Corpus minus Houston spread is the basin's swing signal.

corridors.label: Eagle Ford to Houston
corridors.note: About 250 miles. KMCC barrels are Houston-committed; JV barrels can swing here through the Lyssy interconnect.

notes: The definitional trap, printed: the Texas RRC counts oil leases only and reports condensate separately; EIA counts crude plus lease condensate together. The statewide July 2026 illustration: RRC crude 3,920 against EIA Texas field production of about 5,770 for the same month. This feed's supply card is EIA's combined figure. The RRC-category items ship without values because the RRC pull does not exist in the library; comparing the two counters without the bridge compares different liquids.

Supply footing: the card (1,110) is EIA's control total and the item list sums to zero valued items, on purpose. The split of the combined figure into oil-lease crude and gas-lease condensate lives only in the RRC data that has not been pulled. The gap register names the unlock.

Nameplate arithmetic, with the caveat on the card: trunk nameplates sum to roughly 1,900 to 2,100 including NuStar and smaller systems, against production of 1,110. Two of the biggest numbers are shared: the Eagle Ford JV south of Gardendale also carries Permian Cactus barrels, and the Ingleside Pipeline's 600 is a terminal-delivery leg fed by 380 of Harvest barrels plus Permian connections, not additive takeaway.

Effective capacity for Eagle Ford barrels is refused as a single number, on purpose: the shared segments are rationed by Permian flows that run at or near full utilisation, so the derate is real and it moves monthly. Printing one figure would fabricate precision.

What binds in this basin is not pipe capacity. It is quality (a 45 API crude and a 55 API condensate meeting a system built around Permian WTI at 42 to 44 API; the lightest barrels clear through about 200 of splitter capacity at Corpus and Galena Park, blending, or discount) and queue position at shared Corpus infrastructure (about 2,400 of Permian crude targets the same docks and some of the same steel).

Demand card is blank on purpose: demand items carry verified capacity, and no flow layer exists for this basin in held data. Corpus refining capacity adjacent to the basin is about 832 (Flint Hills West 290 and East 87.5, Valero 290, Citgo 165), and Corpus port crude loadings run about 2,400, mostly Permian barrels in the same tanks; neither is an Eagle Ford demand value.

Name trap, documented: 'Eagle Ford Midstream' is a 158-mile natural gas residue pipeline to Agua Dulce that never touches crude. The crude-relevant system is EFS Midstream, the Pioneer and Reliance gathering and stabilization system sold to Enterprise in 2015. This feed carries the function under its asset owners, never under the ambiguous name.

Decline treadmill: legacy decline consumes roughly 120 to 155 of new production every month, completions run about 119 a month, and the drilled-but-uncompleted inventory is a few months of work (about 310 to 417 depending on the counter). Supply surprises here come from activity decisions by a consolidating operator set, not geology headlines. Peak was about 1,600 to 1,700 in 2015.
Houston's 45-foot channel caps it at Suezmax loadings, one structural reason Corpus took the export crown while Houston kept the pricing role.
